issues.title: Proposed Addition — Section 9.2: Residual Vulnerability Surface in Retained Implementations
issues.author: kayodeelekula123
issues.body:
The draft identifies Edgeless Systems Contrast and Meta's AI as the two early-attestation implementations that remain unarchived (Sec. 9). Section 9 states they "remain vulnerable," citing (a) violation of the SEAT charter requirement to bind to the connection and (b) for Contrast, reliance on the vendor for hardware identifiers. The draft does not specify verification criteria by which such implementations could be reassessed. This subsection supplies them.

Residual Risk Criteria for Retained Early-Attestation Implementations

An implementation of early attestation should be classified as vulnerable until all four criteria are demonstrably satisfied:

1. Binder derivation. The binder is derived from a shared secret established in the handshake (g^xy or a key derived from it). Table 11 establishes that mechanisms 1, 2, 4, and 6 fail G1 and that all analyzed mechanisms fail G3. Verification requires inspection of the binder construction, not the evidence format. Applicability to both retained implementations: confirmed via the G1/G3 failure established in [Intra-handshake.fail].
2. Hardware identifier trust path. The relying party obtains legitimate PIIDs and CHIP_IDs through a path that does not require trusting the vendor. A vendor-mediated path places the vendor inside the TCB regardless of binder correctness. Applicability to Contrast: confirmed in Sec. 9. Applicability to Meta's AI: not stated in the draft and should be assessed.
3. Evidence-data completeness. Evidence with nil, empty, or omitted reportData must be rejected. CVE-2026-92702 and GHSA-Cocos-AI3 establish this as a failure mode distinct from binder weakness: an implementation can satisfy criterion 1 and still accept unattested data. Applicability to the two retained implementations: not established in the draft and should be assessed per implementation.
4. Policy substitution resistance. Generated policies must detect all image substitutions. CVE-2026-100833 and GHSA-Edgeless-Systems6 establish this as orthogonal to cryptographic binding. Applicability to Contrast: confirmed (CVE-2026-100833 is a Contrast CVE; patched in 1.23.1 per the draft). Applicability to Meta's AI: not stated and should be assessed.

Application

For each retained implementation, the draft should record which criteria are satisfied, which are unverified, and the date of last assessment. Without such a record, the "remain vulnerable" statement in Section 9 rests on criteria 1 and 2 (the latter confirmed only for Contrast) and does not address criteria 3 and 4. Separating confirmed from unverified applicability makes the claim precise and gives each vendor a concrete remediation target.

issues.title: . 9.3 declaration criterion and survey boundary
issues.author: kayodeelekula123
issues.body:
9.3. Declaration Criterion and Survey Boundary

This draft makes two class-level claims that require an explicit classification rule and a defined survey boundary to be auditable:

- Abstract: “all except two implementations of early attestation have been archived, withdrawn, or moved to post-handshake attestation.”
- Section 9: “the remaining two implementations of early attestation — Edgeless Systems Contrast and Meta's AI — remain vulnerable.”

Neither claim is accompanied by (a) an explicit declaration criterion specifying what evidence suffices to classify an implementation as vulnerable, or (b) a defined survey boundary specifying the population over which “all except two” is asserted.

Proposed declaration criterion. An implementation of early attestation is classified as vulnerable under this draft if and only if at least one of the following criteria is demonstrated to apply:

- D1 — Binder failure. The binder is not derived from a shared secret, thereby violating G1 as defined in Table 11. This failure must be demonstrated through formal analysis (e.g., [Intra-handshake.fail-repo]) or code inspection establishing the absence of the required secret-dependent derivation.

- D2 — Evidence-data acceptance. The implementation accepts attestation evidence whose "reportData" is nil, empty, or omitted, where the protocol requires this field to bind the evidence to the intended session or challenge. This failure must be demonstrated by a reproducible test case (cf. CVE-2026-92702). The finding applies to an implementation only where the relevant behavior has been independently established; a vulnerability reported in another implementation is not, by itself, proof of the same defect.

- D3 — Identifier trust path. The relying party cannot independently obtain or validate legitimate PIIDs and CHIP_IDs without relying on the vendor as a trusted intermediary. This architectural limitation must be established through an architecture review identifying the identifier-provisioning and validation path, the trust anchors, and the party responsible for asserting identifier legitimacy (cf. Section 9, Contrast). The review must distinguish a documented trust assumption from a demonstrated violation of the security requirements defined by this draft.

- D4 — Policy substitution. The surrounding runtime's generated policies fail to detect one or more unauthorized image substitutions that the policy is intended to prevent. This failure must be demonstrated by a reproducible test case (cf. CVE-2026-100833; GHSA-Edgeless-Systems6). D4 concerns a defect in the surrounding runtime rather than necessarily in the attestation binder itself. It is included because Section 2 establishes that a vulnerability in the overall system, rather than in the attestation mechanism alone, can compromise the security of the system as a whole.

These criteria identify distinct failure modes and must not be treated as interchangeable evidence of the same underlying defect. D1 concerns the cryptographic binding property; D2 concerns evidence-data validation and binding; D3 concerns the architectural trust path for identity; and D4 concerns the enforcement of runtime integrity policy. A finding under any one criterion is sufficient to establish the corresponding security deficiency, provided that the criterion's stated conditions are demonstrated.

An implementation is classified as not demonstrated vulnerable under D1–D4 only when each criterion has been assessed against the relevant implementation and version, and none has been found to apply. A criterion that has not been assessed must be recorded as not assessed, rather than treated as evidence of security. This classification is limited to D1–D4 and does not establish the absence of vulnerabilities outside their scope.

Proposed survey boundary. The claim “all except two” applies to the population of open-source early-attestation implementations surveyed in this draft and enumerated in Table 3 and Section 9.1. The draft should explicitly identify this population as the scope of the authors' survey, rather than imply an exhaustive census of every implementation that may exist. The survey should identify the basis for inclusion and the implementation versions or repository states examined, where available. Consistent with Section 9's existing request for disclosure of undisclosed implementations, the authors should invite corrections, additional implementations, and evidence that may change the classification.

Application to the two retained implementations. Applying the criteria to the findings reported in Section 9 yields the following evidence record:

- Edgeless Systems Contrast: D1 is reported as established (§9, CVE-2026-33697); D3 is reported as established (§9, vendor-mediated identifiers); and D4 is reported as established (CVE-2026-100833, with a fix in version 1.23.1 as reported in §9). D2 is not stated in the cited discussion and therefore remains not established by the evidence presented there. The D4 finding should be scoped to the affected runtime version and should not, by itself, be interpreted as proof of a binder defect in versions containing the fix.

- Meta's AI: D1 is reported as established (§9, CVE-2026-33697). D2, D3, and D4 are not stated in the cited discussion and therefore remain not established by the evidence presented there. Their status must not be inferred from findings concerning Contrast or another implementation without implementation-specific evidence.

Recording which criteria are established, which have been assessed without finding the specified defect, and which remain unassessed converts the Section 9 claim from a generalized assertion into an auditable, implementation-specific classification. It also identifies the relevant remediation target for each demonstrated deficiency without conflating cryptographic, evidence-validation, identity-trust, and runtime-policy failures. Explicitly bounding the survey to the population examined by the authors makes the Abstract's “all except two” claim reproducible and open to correction, without implying a complete census of all existing implementations.  See another

comments.author: phiomegaruntime-rgb
comments.body:
Hi Usama,
I re-read the current draft and also re-ran the problem through the updated
PHI-INFINITY mechanics.
I think there is one narrow property that may strengthen the distinction
between failed intra-handshake binding and later post-handshake attestation:
Post-handshake evidence is non-retroactive: it may establish a new
application-scope relation, but it cannot repair an earlier intra-handshake
binding failure or promote that failed relation across scopes; the earlier
failure and its provenance must remain preserved.
A simple falsification test would be:
establish an intra-handshake binding result as failed or unresolved;
later establish a valid post-handshake/application-scope attestation;
verify that the later valid relation does not reclassify the earlier failed
binding as valid.
In short:
B_application = VALID must not imply B_handshake = VALID.
This seems distinct from G1/G2/G3, freshness, re-attestation and entropy
provenance because it concerns preservation of the status and provenance of
an earlier failed relation across scopes.
If you think this distinction is useful, I can help formulate it directly
in the draft language and place it where it fits best.

pulls.title: Clarify ongoing governability in Agent2Agent interactions
pulls.author: ECMW
pulls.body:
Summary

This PR clarifies the governance implications of the findings for Agent2Agent interactions.

It distinguishes point-in-time attestation evidence from the continuing ability to govern agent interactions, particularly when authority, permissions, or delegation change over time.

The addition highlights the importance of authorization boundaries, attribution, monitoring, and timely intervention, including suspension or revocation.

Scope

These are operational governance considerations, not additional security properties established by the formal analysis in this draft.

The proposed change does not extend the formal security claims beyond what the technical analysis demonstrates.

An implementation of early attestation should be classified as vulnerable until all four criteria are demonstrably satisfied:

1. Binder derivation. The binder is derived from a shared secret established in the handshake (g^xy or a key derived from it). Table 11 establishes that mechanisms 1, 2, 4, and 6 fail G1 and that all analyzed mechanisms fail G3. Verification requires inspection of the binder construction, not the evidence format. Applicability to both retained implementations: confirmed via the G1/G3 failure established in [Intra-handshake.fail].
2. Hardware identifier trust path. The relying party obtains legitimate PIIDs and CHIP_IDs through a path that does not require trusting the vendor. A vendor-mediated path places the vendor inside the TCB regardless of binder correctness. Applicability to Contrast: confirmed in Sec. 9. Applicability to Meta's AI: not stated in the draft and should be assessed.
3. Evidence-data completeness. Evidence with nil, empty, or omitted reportData must be rejected. CVE-2026-92702 and GHSA-Cocos-AI3 establish this as a failure mode distinct from binder weakness: an implementation can satisfy criterion 1 and still accept unattested data. Applicability to the two retained implementations: not established in the draft and should be assessed per implementation.
4. Policy substitution resistance. Generated policies must detect all image substitutions. CVE-2026-100833 and GHSA-Edgeless-Systems6 establish this as orthogonal to cryptographic binding. Applicability to Contrast: confirmed (CVE-2026-100833 is a Contrast CVE; patched in 1.23.1 per the draft). Applicability to Meta's AI: not stated and should be assessed.

Application

For each retained implementation, the draft should record which criteria are satisfied, which are unverified, and the date of last assessment. Without such a record, the "remain vulnerable" statement in Section 9 rests on criteria 1 and 2 (the latter confirmed only for Contrast) and does not address criteria 3 and 4. Separating confirmed from unverified applicability makes the claim precise and gives each vendor a concrete remediation target.

pulls.title: Section 9.3 declaration criterion and survey boundary
pulls.author: kayodeelekula123
pulls.body:
9.3. Declaration Criterion and Survey Boundary

This draft makes two class-level claims that require an explicit classification rule and a defined survey boundary to be auditable:

- Abstract: “all except two implementations of early attestation have been archived, withdrawn, or moved to post-handshake attestation.”
- Section 9: “the remaining two implementations of early attestation — Edgeless Systems Contrast and Meta's AI — remain vulnerable.”

Neither claim is accompanied by (a) an explicit declaration criterion specifying what evidence suffices to classify an implementation as vulnerable, or (b) a defined survey boundary specifying the population over which “all except two” is asserted.

Proposed declaration criterion. An implementation of early attestation is classified as vulnerable under this draft if and only if at least one of the following criteria is demonstrated to apply:

- D1 — Binder failure. The binder is not derived from a shared secret, thereby violating G1 as defined in Table 11. This failure must be demonstrated through formal analysis (e.g., [Intra-handshake.fail-repo]) or code inspection establishing the absence of the required secret-dependent derivation.

- D2 — Evidence-data acceptance. The implementation accepts attestation evidence whose "reportData" is nil, empty, or omitted, where the protocol requires this field to bind the evidence to the intended session or challenge. This failure must be demonstrated by a reproducible test case (cf. CVE-2026-92702). The finding applies to an implementation only where the relevant behavior has been independently established; a vulnerability reported in another implementation is not, by itself, proof of the same defect.

- D3 — Identifier trust path. The relying party cannot independently obtain or validate legitimate PIIDs and CHIP_IDs without relying on the vendor as a trusted intermediary. This architectural limitation must be established through an architecture review identifying the identifier-provisioning and validation path, the trust anchors, and the party responsible for asserting identifier legitimacy (cf. Section 9, Contrast). The review must distinguish a documented trust assumption from a demonstrated violation of the security requirements defined by this draft.

- D4 — Policy substitution. The surrounding runtime's generated policies fail to detect one or more unauthorized image substitutions that the policy is intended to prevent. This failure must be demonstrated by a reproducible test case (cf. CVE-2026-100833; GHSA-Edgeless-Systems6). D4 concerns a defect in the surrounding runtime rather than necessarily in the attestation binder itself. It is included because Section 2 establishes that a vulnerability in the overall system, rather than in the attestation mechanism alone, can compromise the security of the system as a whole.

These criteria identify distinct failure modes and must not be treated as interchangeable evidence of the same underlying defect. D1 concerns the cryptographic binding property; D2 concerns evidence-data validation and binding; D3 concerns the architectural trust path for identity; and D4 concerns the enforcement of runtime integrity policy. A finding under any one criterion is sufficient to establish the corresponding security deficiency, provided that the criterion's stated conditions are demonstrated.

An implementation is classified as not demonstrated vulnerable under D1–D4 only when each criterion has been assessed against the relevant implementation and version, and none has been found to apply. A criterion that has not been assessed must be recorded as not assessed, rather than treated as evidence of security. This classification is limited to D1–D4 and does not establish the absence of vulnerabilities outside their scope.

Proposed survey boundary. The claim “all except two” applies to the population of open-source early-attestation implementations surveyed in this draft and enumerated in Table 3 and Section 9.1. The draft should explicitly identify this population as the scope of the authors' survey, rather than imply an exhaustive census of every implementation that may exist. The survey should identify the basis for inclusion and the implementation versions or repository states examined, where available. Consistent with Section 9's existing request for disclosure of undisclosed implementations, the authors should invite corrections, additional implementations, and evidence that may change the classification.

Application to the two retained implementations. Applying the criteria to the findings reported in Section 9 yields the following evidence record:

- Edgeless Systems Contrast: D1 is reported as established (§9, CVE-2026-33697); D3 is reported as established (§9, vendor-mediated identifiers); and D4 is reported as established (CVE-2026-100833, with a fix in version 1.23.1 as reported in §9). D2 is not stated in the cited discussion and therefore remains not established by the evidence presented there. The D4 finding should be scoped to the affected runtime version and should not, by itself, be interpreted as proof of a binder defect in versions containing the fix.

- Meta's AI: D1 is reported as established (§9, CVE-2026-33697). D2, D3, and D4 are not stated in the cited discussion and therefore remain not established by the evidence presented there. Their status must not be inferred from findings concerning Contrast or another implementation without implementation-specific evidence.

Recording which criteria are established, which have been assessed without finding the specified defect, and which remain unassessed converts the Section 9 claim from a generalized assertion into an auditable, implementation-specific classification. It also identifies the relevant remediation target for each demonstrated deficiency without conflating cryptographic, evidence-validation, identity-trust, and runtime-policy failures. Explicitly bounding the survey to the population examined by the authors makes the Abstract's “all except two” claim reproducible and open to correction, without implying a complete census of all existing implementations.

pulls.title: Support for the Non-Existence Claim: Hybrid vs. Post-Handshake Attestation (§14.1)
pulls.author: kayodeelekula123
pulls.body:
§14.1 — Support for the Non-Existence Claim

The claim "we are not aware of any security property that hybrid proposals can achieve that post-handshake attestation alone cannot achieve" is supported by the following evidence in the draft:

1. Table 11. G1 is achieved by mechanisms 3, 5, 7 and by the proposed mechanism. G2 is achieved only by the proposed mechanism. G3 is achieved by none of the analyzed mechanisms. Post-handshake attestation achieves G1 and G2. Intra-handshake alone achieves G1 only. No analyzed hybrid combination achieves a property that post-handshake alone does not.
2. §3.3. The intra-handshake binder in [I-D.fossati-seat-early-attestation] does not prevent relay attacks because it contains no shared secret. Adding post-handshake attestation to that binder does not change the binder; the intra-handshake path retains the flaw. The hybrid carries the intra-handshake vulnerability without gaining a property.
3. §10 and Table 10. [I-D.fossati-tls-attestation-10] was withdrawn, [I-D.ritz-seat-facts] was archived, and [I-D.fossati-seat-early-attestation] is vulnerable. The three hybrid specifications submitted to the working group either failed the G3 analysis or were withdrawn.
4. §18.2.1, question 1. The question was put to working group participants: what security property does hybrid provide that post-handshake alone cannot? No answer was produced in the archived thread over the review period documented in §20.1.1 (2 Dec 2025 through 5 Oct 2026).
5. §14.4 and §18.2.2. Each of the four MUST requirements is satisfied by post-handshake attestation, requirement by requirement:
   · Evidence MUST be bound to the secure channel. Post-handshake attestation binds evidence to the secure channel after the handshake, without the intra-handshake path.
   · Verifier MUST have access to legitimate hardware identifiers. This requirement concerns the verifier's identifier source, not the timing of attestation. Post-handshake attestation does not change the identifier source and does not require the intra-handshake path.
   · Verifier MUST carefully check the binding. This requirement concerns verifier behavior, not the timing of attestation. Post-handshake attestation does not require the intra-handshake path to satisfy it.
   · Binder MUST contain shared secrets. Post-handshake attestation binds to the established shared secret; it does not require the intra-handshake binder.

None of the four requirements requires the intra-handshake path.

The claim is bounded by the properties analyzed in this draft, namely G1, G2, and G3. The evidence above establishes that none of G1–G3 requires the hybrid.
